title: Topics grid dropped the queued ghost cell of the widest topic row
body:
## Summary
The topics grid sized itself from max_videos (finished videos only), so the widest row's queued/rendering ghost cell at ordinal videos+1 was never drawn.

## Description
apps/server/src/topics.ts:225 computes max_videos from videos.length; apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapTopics.tsx:43 passed it straight to visibleColumns, and TopicLine draws the ghost only at `o === next` (apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapTopics.tsx:224). For the widest row next = max+1 is outside the ordinals, so the most common case (one topic, its next video queued) showed no ghost although the legend lists 'queued / rendering' and data.ts polls every 10 s while anything is pending. Fixed: gridWidth() in apps/studio/src/topicHeatmap.ts adds one column for a row with a pending video. Technique: data-viz/empty-and-degraded-chart-states.

## Flow
- topic with 1 video, its 2nd queued -> max_videos 1 -> ordinals [1] -> ghost at 2 never rendered
- fix: visibleColumns(gridWidth(max_videos, rows)) -> ordinals [1,2] -> ghost drawn

## Expected impact
The owner sees a video they queued appear on the topics grid. Could break: one extra empty column for other rows while a job runs.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the pending state the legend promises is visible
Before: 2 of 2 walked pending rows on the widest topic draw no ghost (seeded red: gridWidth returning max_videos -> 'expected 1 to be 2')
After: 5 of 5 gridWidth cases right; widest row's next ordinal is a drawn column
Method: gate - new test in apps/studio/src/topicHeatmap.test.ts, red on the old behaviour, green on the fix
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/topics.ts:225 max_videos: out.reduce((m, t) => Math.max(m, t.videos.length), 0)
apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapTopics.tsx:43 visibleColumns(data?.max_videos ?? 0)  (before)
apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapTopics.tsx:224 if (o === next && pendingLabel)

title: Cell layer called a failed heatmap load 'No such cell' and offered no retry
body:
## Summary
When GET /api/heatmap failed, the cell layer rendered its not-found state ('No such cell') with the error in the body and no Retry.

## Description
apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapCell.tsx:214-224 (before) merged hm.isError into the `!uc || !cell` branch. A message that names the wrong cause (the cell does not exist) for a request that died, with no action except Back - async-ui-states/failure-states: failure is spelled differently from empty. Fixed: a separate `hm.isError && !hm.data` branch renders the shared <Failure> with Retry (refetch) plus Back to the grid.

## Flow
- open /heatmap/<uc>/<sport> while the API returns 500
- before: 'No such cell' + error text, 0 Retry
- after: 'The heatmap did not load' + error + Retry + Back

## Expected impact
The owner retries instead of concluding the cell is gone. Could break: nothing; the not-found branch is unchanged for a loaded heatmap.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a load failure reads as a failure and can be retried
Before: 1 of 1 failed-load render says 'No such cell', 0 Retry (red)
After: failure heading + 1 Retry; not-found still 'No such cell' (2 of 2)
Method: gate - new apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapCell.test.tsx renders the layer with router/data hooks stubbed
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapCell.tsx:214 ) : !uc || !validSport || !cell ? ( ... No such cell {hm.isError ? `The heatmap did not load: ...` : ...} (before)

title: Unused per-render A/1 flip set; insetFor and bucketOf had no caller
body:
## Summary
HeatmapFeasibility computed `changed` (useMemo over all cells + a no-deps effect rebuilding a Map every render) for FinishSheet, which never reads it; insetFor() and bucketOf() were exported with only their tests as consumers.

## Description
apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapFeasibility.tsx:105-121 (before) - the On Air (A/1) flip animation was retired (ADR 009). apps/studio/src/heatmap.ts:183 insetFor (the layer clips with its own clipFrom/clipFull); apps/studio/src/topicHeatmap.ts:12 bucketOf (pass-through of bucketForAge, whose boundaries packages/schemas/src/topics.test.ts already pins).

## Flow
- grep changed -> declared, computed, passed, never read
- grep insetFor|bucketOf -> definitions + tests only
- remove all three and their tests/imports

## Expected impact
Less work per Feasibility render, two fewer dead exports. Could break: nothing calls them.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - per-render work and dead exports
Before: 2 O(cells) passes + 1 Map rebuild per render; 2 dead exports
After: 0 / 0 (47 lines removed)
Method: gate - tsc + vitest green after removal; zero-consumer grep in evidence
Result: better
Gate: none

## Summary

title: Cell-layer close timer is never cleared; leaving within it yanks the owner back
body:
## Summary
close() schedules navigate('/heatmap') after the close animation with an uncleared setTimeout; navigating elsewhere inside that window returns the owner to the heatmap.

## Description
apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapCell.tsx:128 window.setTimeout(done, dur) (dur = --motion-base, 300 ms); no cleanup on unmount, and closing.current stays true. A click on a nav link during the close animation unmounts the layer, then done() fires and navigates to /heatmap. Fix: keep the timer id in a ref and clear it on unmount.

## Flow
- press Esc on a cell, then click Calendar in the nav within 300 ms
- route goes to /calendar, then back to /heatmap
- fix: clear the timer on unmount

## Expected impact
No surprise navigation. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no stray navigation after unmount
Before: 1 walked race reproduces by reading
After: not taken
Method: simulation - the timer and unmount order walked; instrument named
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: fake-timer test: call close(), unmount, advance 300 ms -> navigate calls 1 -> 0

title: Rescheduling a missed slot defaulted to the time it already missed
body:
## Summary

## Flow
- a slot misses at 09:00, owner opens Calendar at 12:20
- before: input 09:00, warning shown, Reschedule re-misses
- after: input 13:00, no warning

## Expected impact

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the default recovery action succeeds
Before: 1 of 1 missed slot opens on its past time (seeded red)
After: next full hour, 0 warnings from checkSchedule; scheduled slots unchanged

Result: better

title: Metrics watch time under 30 s prints '0 min'
body:
## Summary
The Watch time column rounds seconds to whole minutes, so a publication with 1-29 s of watch time reads '0 min' - a measured non-zero shown as zero.

## Description
apps/studio/src/routes/Metrics.tsx:160 `${fmtNum(Math.round(p.watch_time_s / 60))} min` while the Avg view column uses fmtDuration (m:ss). status-vocabulary/number-formatting: a figure must not misstate its value. Which unit to use for small values is a small format call (m:ss below a minute vs one decimal).

## Flow
- a short with 3 views x 8 s
- watch_time_s 24 -> '0 min'
- fix: m:ss under an hour, or '< 1 min'

## Expected impact
Small numbers read honestly once live metrics exist. Could break: column width.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - non-zero figures never read as zero
Before: 1-29 s -> '0 min' (read)
After: not taken
Method: simulation - three values walked (24 s, 89 s, 3600 s); live metrics do not exist yet (dry runs)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: pure fmtWatch() with a test over 0, 24, 89, 3600 s; values misreported 1 -> 0
